DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

Water on Trial

STS-HS11-L3-BR300-HSSCIENG1112-CPO-GBL-01 • HS Science Engineering Design 11-12 • Applying Scientific Knowledge to Design a Solution
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
In a court of public opinion, a design does not win because it is clever. It wins because the people who must live with it agree that it works. Amara, Nikhil, and Mei took one large problem, clean water at school, and cut it into three smaller ones: collect it, filter it, carry it. Tonight students at their partner schools in five countries vote on the same three panels.
The filter passes its test, but the full tank weighs 20 kg and no one student can carry it. Which of the three smaller problems would you solve next, and how?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Amara doing?
Look at the picture. Say: Amara is ____. (pouring • cleaning) Then say why she does it. What is the machine for?
2
What is Nikhil holding?
Look at the picture. Say: Nikhil is holding ____. (a glass of water • a bag) Then say why he holds it up. What should people see?
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Say: The teacher is ____. (voting • drawing) Then say why. What does the box decide?
4
What place is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Say: This is a ____. (courtroom • park) Then say how you know. What do you see in the room?
5
Tell me about the board behind them.
Look at the picture. Say: The board has ____ parts. (three • nine) Then say why. What is each part for?
6
What is Mei wearing?
Look at the picture. Say: Mei is wearing a ____ coat. (yellow • brown) Then say one more thing about her clothes. Which clothes are easy to see from far away?
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
Content alignment: HS-ETS1-2 — Apply scientific knowledge to design a solution to a complex real world problem, breaking it down into smaller, more manageable problems. ELD (Speaking — official ELPAC “Talk About a Scene”): PI.A.1, PII.B.3, PII.B.4, PII.B.5.
